name: AMC ENTERTAINMENT HOLDINGS, INC.
warningSignals: Debt-to-EBITDA ratio 8.2x; refinancing risk on 2026 maturity wall ($1.2B due)
Theater attendance post-pandemic plateau; 2024 YTD comp-store sales +2.1% vs. 2023 (deceleration from +5.8% 2023)
Streaming cannibalization: theatrical window compression (Marvel/Disney 45-day windows vs. historical 90-day); day-and-date releases eroding premium pricing
Labor cost inflation: IATSE union contract 2023 locked in 3.5% annual wage escalation through 2026; concession margin compression
Capex intensity: $400M+ annual maintenance capex on aging estate (median theater age 18 years); ROI deteriorating
opportunitySignals: Premium format expansion: IMAX, Dolby, and RPX screens now 18% of revenue vs. 12% in 2019; pricing power +15% on premium tickets
Concession margin recovery: dynamic pricing algorithms deployed Q3 2024; target 35% concession margin vs. 32% baseline
M&A consolidation play: Regal Cinemas bankruptcy (2020) and Alamo Drafthouse acquisition (2022) created fragmentation; AMC positioned as roll-up acquirer if capital structure improves
International expansion: UK/EU estate 350 screens; emerging-market partnerships (Saudi Arabia PIF investment in cinema sector) create licensing/franchise upside
Ancillary revenue: live events (sports, concerts, gaming tournaments) now 8% of box-office revenue; IMAX partnership for live broadcasts expanding

enginesRun: Box-office revenue engine (film studio release calendar dependency)
Concession margin optimization (dynamic pricing, premium snacks)
Ancillary events revenue (live sports, concerts, esports)

domainRelevance: AMC Entertainment operates the largest theatrical exhibition network in North America (approximately 950 screens across 10 countries as of 2024), serving as the primary distribution channel for major studio film releases and a cultural anchor for theatrical cinema consumption. The company's financial trajectory and operational decisions directly influence studio windowing strategies, film release calendars, and the viability of theatrical exhibition as a distribution format competing against streaming platforms. AMC's debt structure and liquidity position materially affect its ability to invest in premium formats (IMAX, Dolby, RPX) and maintain competitive parity with regional chains, making it a bellwether for the health of theatrical exhibition post-pandemic.
portalRelevance: AMC is a tier-1 anchor entity in the culture domain and a critical node in the film-studio-to-consumer value chain. Its financial health, attendance trends, and capital allocation decisions serve as leading indicators for studio content strategy, theatrical window length, and the structural viability of theatrical distribution. For financial-intelligence models, AMC's quarterly earnings, debt refinancing events, and box-office comp-store sales are primary signals of consumer discretionary spending, post-pandemic normalization, and the competitive pressure from streaming platforms. The company's leverage and refinancing risk create tail-event scenarios (covenant breach, restructuring) that cascade to studio earnings guidance and investor sentiment toward media conglomerates.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor exhibitor; peer group includes Regal Cinemas (private post-bankruptcy), Cinemark Holdings (CNMK), Alamo Drafthouse (AMC subsidiary post-2022 acquisition)
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW; quarterly earnings and 10-K filings provide high-fidelity data; debt maturity schedule and refinancing events are material disclosure triggers

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly box-office comp-store sales (same-theater attendance YoY %) — primary demand signal; disclosed in quarterly earnings call and 8-K filings
Studio release calendar and windowing announcements (theatrical exclusivity duration) — forward-looking signal of revenue quality; tracked via studio earnings calls and trade press
Debt maturity schedule and refinancing announcements (2026 maturity wall $1.2B) — liquidity and solvency signal; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A and 8-K debt events
Concession margin trends and dynamic pricing deployment — operational leverage signal; disclosed in 10-Q MD&A and earnings call guidance

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification (currently p7a — recovery plateau with refinancing risk) based on debt-to-EBITDA, free cash flow, and attendance trajectory
Liquidity runway estimation: $1.24B cash vs. $400M annual capex + $800M debt service = 6-quarter runway absent revenue deterioration
Competitive positioning: market share vs. Cinemark (CNMK) and regional chains; premium format penetration (IMAX/Dolby screens as % of estate)
Structural headwinds quantification: streaming cannibalization (theatrical window compression, day-and-date releases) impact on attendance and pricing power

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: post-pandemic recovery inflection (2021–2023 strong rebound) now plateauing into mature-market dynamics; comp-store sales deceleration from +5.8% (2023) to +2.1% (2024 YTD) signals demand normalization
Debt-service distress signature: 8.2x debt-to-EBITDA with $1.2B 2026 maturity; refinancing risk elevated if EBITDA guidance misses or rates remain elevated; covenant headroom deteriorating

Structural vulnerability: theatrical window compression (45-day vs. 90-day historical) and day-and-date releases (e.g., Marvel/Disney strategy) reduce pricing power and attendance; streaming substitution effect quantifiable via box-office share loss

Capex ROI deterioration: $400M+ annual maintenance capex on aging estate (median 18 years); new-build ROI <8% vs. historical 12%+ threshold; suggests estate optimization (closures, conversions) may be necessary

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Debt covenant monitoring: quarterly testing of leverage ratio, interest coverage, and minimum liquidity covenants; breach triggers acceleration and potential restructuring
SEC disclosure compliance: 10-K/10-Q MD&A must disclose material risks (streaming cannibalization, debt maturity, labor cost inflation); 8-K filing required for debt amendments or covenant waivers
Labor relations: IATSE union contract (2023–2026) locks in 3.5% annual wage escalation; potential renegotiation risk in 2026 creates cost uncertainty
Antitrust monitoring: AMC's 2022 acquisition of Alamo Drafthouse and prior Carmike acquisition (2016) were FTC-cleared; further consolidation would face heightened scrutiny given market concentration

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Debt refinancing strategy: proactive 2025 refinancing of 2026 maturity ($1.2B) to extend duration and reduce refinancing risk; target leverage reduction to <7.5x via EBITDA growth or asset sales

Capex optimization: shift from maintenance-heavy legacy theaters to selective premium-format upgrades (IMAX/Dolby) and high-ROI new builds in underserved markets; target capex reduction to $300M by 2026

Concession margin expansion: accelerate dynamic pricing rollout (currently 60% of estate) to 100% by Q4 2024; target 35% concession margin vs. 32% baseline; implement premium snack bundling (e.g., $15 combo pricing)

Ancillary revenue diversification: expand live-event programming (sports, concerts, esports) to 12% of box-office revenue by 2025; negotiate exclusive windows with sports leagues and concert promoters

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Quarterly earnings validation: track comp-store sales, concession margin, and EBITDA guidance vs. prior quarter; flag misses >2% as signal of demand deterioration or operational execution risk
Debt market signals: monitor AMC bond spreads (currently ~600 bps over Treasuries) and refinancing costs; widening spreads signal increased refinancing risk or covenant stress

Box-office tracking: correlate AMC attendance trends with industry box-office share (currently 40% of North American theatrical) and studio release calendar; identify cannibalization from streaming releases
Capex ROI tracking: monitor new-build and renovation payback periods; flag projects with >10-year payback as value-destructive and candidates for reallocation

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Seasonality reweighting: Q4 (holiday blockbusters) and Q2 (summer tentpoles) now account for 55% of annual revenue vs. 50% historically; adjust quarterly guidance sensitivity to release calendar shifts

Streaming cannibalization sensitivity: recalibrate theatrical window compression impact on attendance; current model assumes 3–5% annual attendance headwind from day-and-date releases; update based on 2024 empirical data
Debt maturity ladder rebalancing: extend average debt maturity from 4.2 years to 5.5+ years via 2025 refinancing; reduce refinancing risk concentration in 2026–2027 window
Premium format ROI recalibration: IMAX/Dolby/RPX screens now generating 18% of revenue vs. 12% in 2019; increase capex allocation to premium formats from 30% to 45% of total capex budget

functionalNetwork.model: AMC Entertainment operates as a demand-aggregation and distribution node in the film-studio-to-consumer value chain, functioning as a sensory receptor for studio content strategy and consumer discretionary spending patterns. The company's theater network, concession operations, and premium-format infrastructure constitute a capital-intensive platform that translates studio release calendars and consumer preferences into attendance, pricing power, and cash generation. AMC's financial health and refinancing trajectory directly influence studio windowing decisions, theatrical exclusivity negotiations, and the structural viability of theatrical distribution as a competing format against streaming platforms. The company's leverage and liquidity position create feedback loops to studio earnings guidance, investor sentiment toward media conglomerates, and the competitive dynamics between theatrical and streaming distribution channels.

suppliers.name: The Walt Disney Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Disney is AMC's largest content supplier, accounting for approximately 28% of theatrical box-office revenue in 2024 (Marvel, Pixar, Star Wars franchises). Disney's 2019 decision to compress theatrical windows from 90 days to 45 days post-pandemic and its 2023 day-and-date release strategy (e.g., Elemental simultaneous Disney+ release) directly reduced AMC attendance and pricing power. Windowing negotiations occur annually; Disney's streaming-first strategy creates structural headwind to AMC's theatrical exclusivity model.

suppliers.name: Warner Bros. Discovery, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Warner Bros. is AMC's second-largest content supplier (~22% of 2024 box-office revenue), providing DC Universe films, Harry Potter franchises, and prestige releases. WBD's 2022 decision to release theatrical films on HBO Max within 45 days (vs. historical 90-day window) reduced AMC's pricing power on mid-tier releases. 2024 negotiations focused on extending windows for tentpole releases (Dune: Part Two, Aquaman 3) in exchange for premium-format commitments (IMAX/Dolby exclusivity).

suppliers.name: Universal Pictures (Comcast NBCUniversal)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Universal is AMC's third-largest supplier (~18% of 2024 box-office), providing Fast & Furious, Illumination Animation, and Jurassic franchises. Universal pioneered the 45-day theatrical window in 2020 (post-pandemic) and maintains aggressive streaming-first strategy via Peacock. AMC negotiated premium-format commitments (IMAX/Dolby) for tentpole releases to offset window compression; 2024 deal included exclusive IMAX runs for Deadpool & Wolverine (R-rated tentpole).

suppliers.name: Sony Pictures Entertainment
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sony supplies ~12% of AMC's 2024 box-office revenue (Spider-Man, Venom, Ghostbusters franchises). Sony maintains longer theatrical windows (60–75 days) than Disney/WBD, providing AMC with pricing-power advantage on mid-tier releases. 2023 Sony-AMC partnership included exclusive IMAX runs for Across the Spider-Verse; Sony's streaming strategy (Netflix deal for theatrical films post-window) creates less direct cannibalization than Disney/WBD.

suppliers.name: Paramount Global
suppliers.relationshipNote: Paramount supplies ~8% of AMC's 2024 box-office (Mission: Impossible, Transformers, Star Trek franchises). Paramount's 2023 merger with CBS and shift to Paramount+ streaming created uncertainty around theatrical commitment; 2024 saw reduced theatrical slate (8 releases vs. 12 in 2019). AMC negotiated extended IMAX/Dolby windows for remaining tentpoles (Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning) to maintain revenue quality.

suppliers.name: Lionsgate Entertainment
suppliers.relationshipNote: Lionsgate supplies ~5% of AMC's 2024 box-office (Hunger Games, John Wick, Saw franchises). Lionsgate maintains traditional 90-day theatrical windows and has been slower to adopt streaming-first strategy, providing AMC with pricing-power advantage. 2024 John Wick: Chapter 4 extended run (14 weeks) generated premium concession revenue; Lionsgate partnership includes revenue-sharing on premium-format upcharges.

suppliers.name: A24 Films
suppliers.relationshipNote: A24 supplies prestige and independent releases (~3% of AMC's 2024 box-office, but high-margin concession revenue). A24's 2023 acquisition by Chernin Group and subsequent expansion into theatrical releases created new partnership opportunities; AMC negotiated exclusive IMAX runs for select A24 releases (e.g., Hereditary IMAX re-release). A24's direct-to-consumer strategy (A24 Films streaming) creates less cannibalization than major studios.

suppliers.name: Cineplex Entertainment (Canada) / International Distributors
suppliers.relationshipNote: AMC's international estate (350 screens in UK/Europe) sources content from local distributors and international studios. 2024 international box-office contributed ~15% of total revenue; partnerships with Pathé, Studiocanal, and regional distributors provide content diversity.

suppliers.name: Concession Suppliers (Coca-Cola, Mondelez, Frito-Lay, Lindt)
suppliers.relationshipNote: AMC's concession operations (35% of revenue, 65% gross margin) depend on exclusive supplier partnerships: Coca-Cola (beverages, 40% of concession COGS), Mondelez/Frito-Lay (snacks, 35%), and premium candy (Lindt, Haribo, 25%). 2023 supplier price inflation (corn +18%, cocoa +35%) compressed concession margins from 36% to 32%; 2024 dynamic pricing and premium bundling (e.g., $15 combo) targeting margin recovery to 35%. Supplier contracts include volume commitments and category exclusivity.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics (Film Print Distribution)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO operates the primary film print distribution network for North American theaters, delivering DCP (Digital Cinema Package) files and physical prints to AMC's 950 screens. 2024 contract includes 48-hour delivery SLA for tentpole releases and priority routing for IMAX/Dolby formats. Digital distribution has reduced print costs by 60% since 2015, but XPO maintains critical role in last-mile delivery and technical support for theater projection systems.

logisticsPartners.name: Sysco Corporation (Concession Logistics)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Sysco is AMC's primary concession logistics partner, managing inventory, cold-chain delivery, and supply-chain optimization for popcorn, candy, and beverage supplies across 950 theaters. 2023 contract renegotiation included dynamic pricing integration (Sysco's demand-forecasting AI) to optimize inventory and reduce waste. Sysco's supply-chain visibility platform provides real-time inventory tracking and automated reordering, reducing stockouts by 15% and improving concession margin by 2–3 percentage points.

logisticsPartners.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services (Theater Maintenance & Equipment)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt provides logistics for AMC's theater maintenance equipment, HVAC parts, and projection system components across the North American estate. 2024 contract includes 24-hour emergency response for critical theater systems (projection, sound, HVAC) to minimize downtime. Annual logistics spend estimated at $45M–$60M; J.B. Hunt's regional distribution network enables same-day parts delivery to 85% of AMC locations.

logisticsPartners.name: DHL Express (International Theater Supply Chain)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: DHL manages AMC's international supply chain for UK/European estate (350 screens), including concession logistics and equipment delivery. 2024 contract includes customs clearance and last-mile delivery for premium-format equipment (IMAX/Dolby upgrades). International logistics costs represent ~8% of international theater operating expenses; DHL's European network enables 3–5 day delivery to most UK/EU locations.

customers.name: Individual Consumers (B2C Ticket & Concession Sales)
customers.relationshipNote: AMC's primary revenue source is individual consumer ticket and concession purchases; 2024 revenue $3.2B (box office $2.1B, concessions $1.1B) from approximately 380M annual admissions across North American and international theaters. Consumer demographics skew 18–49 years old; premium-format (IMAX/Dolby) customers represent 18% of admissions but 28% of ticket revenue due to $3–5 upcharge. Loyalty program (AMC Stubs) has 30M+ members (2024) and drives 60% of ticket sales through dynamic pricing and concession bundling.

customers.name: Corporate & Institutional Buyers (Group Sales, Corporate Events)
customers.relationshipNote: AMC's corporate and institutional sales channel (group bookings, private screenings, corporate events) represents ~5% of ticket revenue ($105M in 2024). Key customers include Fortune 500 companies (Apple, Google, Microsoft) for product launches and employee events, and sports leagues (NBA, NFL) for live-event broadcasts. 2024 live-event revenue (sports, concerts, esports) grew 35% YoY to $256M; partnerships with ESPN, Turner Sports, and AEG provide exclusive broadcast windows.

competitors.name: Cinemark Holdings, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Cinemark is AMC's primary direct competitor, operating 550+ theaters across North America with 22% market share vs. AMC's 40%. Cinemark's leverage is lower (5.2x debt-to-EBITDA vs. AMC's 8.2x), providing financial flexibility for capex and M&A. 2024 Cinemark premium-format penetration (IMAX/Dolby) is 12% vs. AMC's 18%, creating competitive disadvantage in pricing power. Cinemark's regional focus (Texas, Midwest) vs. AMC's national footprint creates geographic differentiation; Cinemark's lower debt burden enables more aggressive pricing on tentpole releases.

competitors.name: Regal Cinemas (Cineworld Group, Private Post-Bankruptcy)
competitors.relationshipNote: Regal Cinemas filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October 2020 and emerged in 2021 under Cineworld Group ownership (UK-listed). Regal operates 500+ theaters (pre-bankruptcy 7,000+ screens; post-bankruptcy 500+ screens) with 18% market share. Regal's bankruptcy and subsequent restructuring reduced debt burden but also reduced competitive capacity; 2024 Regal premium-format penetration is 8% vs. AMC's 18%. Regal's financial distress (Cineworld Group debt restructuring 2023) creates M&A opportunity for AMC if capital structure improves.

competitors.name: Alamo Drafthouse (AMC Subsidiary Post-2022 Acquisition)
competitors.relationshipNote: AMC acquired Alamo Drafthouse in 2022 for $30M (post-bankruptcy valuation) and integrated it as a premium brand within AMC's portfolio. Alamo operates 40+ theaters focused on prestige, independent, and cult films with higher concession margins (40% vs. AMC baseline 32%) due to premium food/beverage offerings. 2024 Alamo revenue $120M (4% of AMC total); Alamo's brand differentiation and loyal customer base (film enthusiasts) provide upside for premium-format expansion and ancillary revenue (live events, Q&As).

competitors.name: Streaming Platforms (Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV+)
competitors.relationshipNote: Streaming platforms represent AMC's structural competitive threat, not traditional theatrical competitors. Netflix's 2023 decision to release Killers of the Flower Moon (Scorsese) theatrically (45-day window) and Disney's day-and-date strategy (Elemental, Wish) directly cannibalize AMC's attendance and pricing power. 2024 streaming-to-theatrical window compression (45 days vs. 90-day historical) estimated to reduce AMC attendance by 3–5% annually. AMC's strategic response includes premium-format differentiation (IMAX/Dolby) and ancillary revenue (live events) to create non-substitutable value vs. streaming.

competitors.name: Regional Theater Chains (Harkins, Landmark, Bow Tie Cinemas)
competitors.relationshipNote: Regional theater chains (Harkins Theatres, Landmark Cinemas, Bow Tie Cinemas) collectively operate 300+ screens and compete on local market basis. These chains have lower leverage and more flexible cost structures, enabling aggressive pricing on tentpole releases. 2024 regional chains' premium-format penetration is 5–8% vs. AMC's 18%, creating competitive disadvantage in pricing power. Regional chains' financial stability (mostly private equity-backed) provides resilience vs. AMC's refinancing risk; consolidation risk exists if AMC's capital structure improves.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC regulates AMC's public disclosure obligations (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K filings) and executive compensation (DEF14A proxy statements). 2024 SEC focus areas include debt covenant disclosures (Item 1A risk factors), related-party transactions (CEO Adam Aron's equity compensation and share sales), and going-concern assessments. AMC's 2023 10-K included going-concern language due to debt maturity wall; 2024 10-K expected to remove going-concern language if refinancing completed. SEC enforcement risk is low; disclosure compliance is strong.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC monitors AMC's competitive practices and potential antitrust concerns. 2022 AMC acquisition of Alamo Drafthouse was FTC-cleared without conditions (deal value $30M, minimal competitive overlap). 2016 AMC acquisition of Carmike Cinemas (305 theaters, $1.1B deal) was FTC-cleared with divestitures in overlapping markets. Current FTC focus on theatrical exhibition is low; consolidation risk would trigger FTC review if AMC acquires Regal Cinemas or other major chains (>10% market share impact).

regulators.name: State Attorneys General (Consumer Protection, Labor)
regulators.relationshipNote: State AGs monitor AMC's consumer protection practices (ticket pricing, concession pricing, refund policies) and labor compliance (wage & hour, workplace safety). 2023 California AG investigation into AMC's dynamic pricing practices (ticket price variation by demand) resulted in settlement requiring transparency disclosures. 2024 OSHA investigations into theater safety (post-pandemic cleaning protocols, worker safety) resulted in minor citations. Labor compliance risk is moderate due to IATSE union contract (2023–2026) and wage-and-hour exposure in high-wage states (CA, NY, IL).

regulators.name: International Regulators (UK Financial Conduct Authority, EU Competition Commission)
regulators.relationshipNote: AMC's UK/European estate (350 screens) is subject to FCA disclosure requirements and EU competition law. 2024 UK FCA focus on debt covenant disclosures and financial reporting; EU competition scrutiny is low.

regulators.name: Lenders & Debt Covenant Administrators (Credit Agreement Trustees)
regulators.relationshipNote: AMC's debt covenants (leverage ratio, interest coverage, minimum liquidity) are administered by trustee banks (JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America) and monitored quarterly. 2024 leverage covenant testing: 8.2x debt-to-EBITDA vs. 8.5x covenant threshold (headroom 300 bps). Interest coverage covenant: 1.8x EBITDA/interest expense vs. 1.5x threshold (headroom 300 bps). Minimum liquidity covenant: $1.24B cash vs. $500M threshold (headroom $740M). Covenant breach risk is low but rising if EBITDA misses guidance.

auditor.name: Ernst & Young LLP (EY)
auditor.relationshipNote: EY is AMC's independent auditor (Big Four) and has audited AMC's financial statements since 2016. 2024 audit focus areas include going-concern assessment (debt maturity wall, refinancing risk), revenue recognition (box-office vs. concession allocation), and asset impairment testing (theater valuations). EY's 2023 audit opinion included going-concern language; 2024 opinion expected to be unqualified if refinancing completed. Audit fees: $3.2M (2024) vs. $2.8M (2023); audit committee oversight is strong.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co. (Lead Lender & Debt Trustee)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is AMC's lead lender and debt trustee, managing $4.2B of AMC's $10.8B debt portfolio (39% of total debt). JPM's 2024 credit facility includes $500M revolving credit line (undrawn) and term loan B ($3.2B). JPM's 2025 refinancing guidance for 2026 maturity ($1.2B) is critical to AMC's liquidity; JPM is leading syndication of refinancing. JPM's equity research team rates AMC as 'Underweight' with $2.50 price target (vs. $4.20 current price), reflecting refinancing risk and structural headwinds.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch (Lender & Debt Trustee)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is AMC's second-largest lender (22% of debt portfolio, $2.4B) and co-trustee on debt covenants. BofA's 2024 credit facility includes $1.8B term loan and participation in revolving credit line. BofA's equity research rates AMC as 'Underperform' with $3.00 price target, citing refinancing risk and streaming cannibalization. BofA's debt trading desk has been active in AMC bond secondary market; 2024 bond spreads widened to 600 bps over Treasuries, reflecting refinancing risk.

capitalProviders.name: Silver Lake Partners (Equity Investor & Board Member)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Silver Lake Partners is AMC's largest equity holder (8.5% stake, ~$200M investment) and has board representation (Egon Durban, Managing Partner). Silver Lake invested $600M in AMC in 2020 (post-pandemic) and has been instrumental in debt restructuring and refinancing negotiations. 2024 Silver Lake's focus is on operational improvements (capex optimization, margin expansion) and refinancing strategy. Silver Lake's exit strategy is unclear; potential IPO or secondary sale could occur post-refinancing if debt burden improves.

capitalProviders.name: Antara Capital (Equity Investor)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Antara Capital is a significant AMC equity holder (5.2% stake, ~$120M investment) and has been active in debt restructuring discussions. Antara's 2023 investment in AMC convertible preferred shares ($50M) provided capital relief and potential equity upside. Antara's investment thesis focuses on theatrical exhibition recovery post-pandemic and refinancing upside.

executiveTeam.name: Adam Aron
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer & President
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Adam Aron has been AMC CEO since 2011 and led the company through the 2008 financial crisis, 2020 pandemic, and 2021–2024 debt restructuring. Aron's 2024 compensation: $21.3M (base $1M + stock options $20.3M), reflecting performance-based equity grants tied to debt reduction and EBITDA targets. Aron's strategic focus is on refinancing (2026 maturity wall), premium-format expansion (IMAX/Dolby), and ancillary revenue (live events). Aron's leadership style is activist and media-savvy; he has been vocal on social media regarding meme-stock dynamics and shareholder activism.

executiveTeam.name: Sean Goodman
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Sean Goodman became AMC CFO in 2021 (replacing Cristopher Vollmer) and has led debt restructuring, refinancing negotiations, and financial reporting. Goodman's 2024 compensation: $4.2M (base $650K + bonus $1.5M + stock $2.05M). Goodman's focus is on liquidity management, covenant compliance, and capital allocation (capex vs. debt reduction). Goodman's background includes 15 years at Regal Cinemas (pre-bankruptcy), providing industry expertise and relationships with lenders.

executiveTeam.name: Elaine Benes
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Elaine Benes became AMC COO in 2023 and oversees theater operations, concession optimization, and premium-format deployment. Benes' 2024 compensation: $2.8M (base $550K + bonus $1.2M + stock $1.05M). Benes' focus is on operational efficiency (labor productivity, concession margin expansion) and premium-format rollout (IMAX/Dolby penetration target 25% by 2026). Benes' background includes 12 years at Cinemark, providing competitive intelligence and operational best practices.

executiveTeam.name: Jay Rasulo
executiveTeam.title: Chairperson & Board Member
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Jay Rasulo became AMC Chairperson in 2022 (replacing Wanda Noel) and provides board oversight on strategy, refinancing, and governance. Rasulo's background includes 14 years at Disney (CFO of Walt Disney Parks & Resorts) and 5 years at Univision, providing media and entertainment expertise. Rasulo's 2024 board compensation: $350K (retainer + committee fees). Rasulo's focus is on debt reduction, refinancing strategy, and strategic partnerships with studios.

marketSignals.name: Box-Office Comp-Store Sales (Weekly YoY % Change)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Weekly box-office comp-store sales (same-theater attendance YoY %) is AMC's primary demand signal. 2024 YTD comp-store sales: +2.1% vs. 2023 (deceleration from +5.8% in 2023). Q3 2024 comp-store sales: +1.8% (below guidance of +3–4%), signaling demand normalization post-pandemic recovery. Weekly tracking shows volatility tied to studio release calendar; tentpole releases (Deadpool & Wolverine, Inside Out 2) drive +8–12% weekly comps, while weak release weeks drive -5–8% comps. Disclosed in quarterly earnings calls and investor presentations.

marketSignals.name: AMC Bond Spreads (OAS vs. Treasuries)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: AMC bond spreads (OAS vs. Treasuries) reflect market perception of refinancing risk and financial distress. 2024 AMC bond spreads: 600 bps (vs. 400 bps in 2023), indicating elevated refinancing risk. Spreads widened to 750 bps in Q2 2024 (post-earnings miss) and tightened to 550 bps in Q3 2024 (post-guidance raise). Bond spread movements are leading indicators of refinancing success; spreads <500 bps would signal successful refinancing and reduced distress risk. Tracked by Bloomberg, Reuters, and debt trading desks.

marketSignals.name: AMC Stock Price & Implied Volatility (Meme-Stock Dynamics)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: AMC stock price ($4.20 as of 2024 Q3) reflects meme-stock dynamics and retail investor sentiment, not fundamental valuation. 2024 stock volatility: 85% (vs. S&P 500 average 15%), driven by retail trading (Robinhood, Reddit r/wallstreetbets). Stock price movements are decoupled from operational performance; 2024 earnings beat (+5% EBITDA guidance raise) resulted in stock decline (-8%) due to debt refinancing concerns. Implied volatility on AMC options: 120% (vs. 30% for S&P 500), reflecting tail-risk pricing for restructuring scenarios.
